open_questions/0.rationale: Epidemiologic data robustly link severe obesity to higher multiple myeloma incidence and mortality, and Fairfield et al. (2026) confirmed in CoMMpass clinical data that moderate-to-severe obesity at diagnosis associates with increased patient mortality and distinct myeloma-cell gene-expression and pathway signatures. They further showed that high-fat-diet obesity accelerated myeloma only in the immune-competent C57BL/6J 5TGM1 semisyngeneic model — not in the SCID-beige xenograft or the Vk*MYC model — implicating the host immune system rather than a tumor-intrinsic effect alone. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unknown: it is unresolved which specific immune populations (T cells, NK cells, macrophages, neutrophils, regulatory T cells) are disrupted, and how obesity-associated adipokines and altered marrow lipid/metabolic flux mechanistically drive plasma-cell survival and proliferation. It is also unclear whether the obesity-altered myeloma-cell gene signatures activate stemness, drug-resistance, or immune-evasion programs. Resolving whether obesity acts primarily through impaired anti-tumor immunity, a permissive adipocyte-rich marrow niche, or tumor-intrinsic reprogramming would clarify whether obesity is a modifiable target for myeloma prevention and which interventions to prioritize.

open_questions/1.rationale: Fairfield et al. (2026) tested three high-fat-diet mouse myeloma systems and found that obesity accelerated disease only in the immune-competent C57BL/6J 5TGM1 semisyngeneic model, not in the immunodeficient SCID-beige xenograft or the Vk*MYC model. The CoMMpass clinical data establish that obesity at diagnosis is associated with increased human mortality and altered myeloma-cell gene-expression signatures, so a human obesity effect is real; the open question is whether the single positive mouse model captures the human mechanism or whether its dependence on an intact immune system and a specific genetic background makes it a partial, model-specific surrogate. The discordance among models is itself mechanistically informative — it implies that obesity acts at least partly through the host immune system rather than a purely tumor-intrinsic route — but it also means mechanistic inferences drawn from the 5TGM1 model may not generalize to the heterogeneous genetic and immune backgrounds of human myeloma. Resolving this is essential before leveraging the model for obesity-targeted prevention or therapy.

steps/3.description: The recurrent NSML PTPN11 missense variants map to the catalytic PTP domain and reduce SHP2 phosphatase activity, in contrast to the activating (gain-of-function) SHP2 alleles that cause Noonan syndrome. steps/4.description: In the RAF1 (LPRD2) and BRAF (LPRD3) arms, the pathogenic variants are activating kinase mutations, in contrast to the catalytically-impaired SHP2 of the PTPN11 arm. evidence.snippet: interfere with growth factor/Erk-mitogen-activated protein kinase-mediated signaling

steps/5.description: NSML-causing variants across PTPN11, RAF1, and BRAF converge on abnormal RAS-MAPK (ERK1/2) pathway output, the unifying mechanism of the RASopathies. In PTPN11-NSML, the catalytically-dead but still-scaffolding SHP2 produces context-dependent, tissue-specific dysregulation rather than uniform loss of signaling.

evidence.snippet: enhanced binding of Shp2 to Irs1, decreased Shp2 catalytic activity, and abrogated agonist-evoked Erk/Mapk signaling. LS/+ mice also exhibited increased basal and agonist-induced Akt and mTor activity

steps/7.description: Aberrant developmental SHP2 signaling and downstream Akt/mTOR activity in cardiomyocytes and endocardium drives concentric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, the hallmark that most distinguishes NSML from classic Noonan syndrome.

evidence.snippet: we identified a homozygous nonsense variant in PUS3; Chr11(GRCh37):g.125763823G>A; NM_031307.3: c.1303C>T: p.(Arg435*) that fully segregated with the phenotype in the family as confirmed by Sanger sequencing
evidence.explanation: Establishes the founding biallelic protein-truncating allele as the initiating lesion.

evidence.snippet: we utilize exome sequencing to identify genomic variants that lead to a homozygous amino acid substitution
evidence.explanation: Documents the missense arm of the allelic spectrum, identified by exome sequencing in two homozygous individuals and one compound heterozygote. The quoted fragment stops before the HGVS allele strings because their square brackets are not preserved in the cached reference text.

steps/1.description: The disorder is initiated by inheritance of two damaging PUS3 alleles. The reported allelic spectrum is broad and includes nonsense alleles that truncate the protein (the founding p.Arg435* allele), frameshift alleles, a splice-region allele, an initiation-codon substitution, and missense alleles. Critically, the missense alleles are not a milder mechanistic class: p.Tyr71Cys retains essentially normal tRNA binding and catalytic activity when the purified protein is assayed, yet behaves as a functional null in cells, so the allelic spectrum converges on one outcome rather than producing a hypomorph gradient.

evidence.snippet: Human pseudouridine synthase 3 (PUS3) catalyzes pseudouridylation of position 38/39 in tRNAs.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the enzyme and the exact catalytic reaction whose loss defines this node.

evidence.snippet: Here, we determine single-particle cryo-EM structures of PUS3 in its apo form and bound to three tRNAs, showing how the symmetric PUS3 homodimer recognizes tRNAs and positions the target uridine next to its active site.
evidence.explanation: Supplies the structural basis for how the enzyme engages its substrate, and therefore what patient alleles disrupt.

evidence.snippet: we find that the p.Tyr71Cys substitution neither affect tRNA binding nor pseudouridylation activity in vitro, but strongly impair the thermostability profile of PUS3, while the p.Ile299Thr mutation causes protein aggregation.
evidence.explanation: Establishes protein destabilisation and aggregation, rather than direct catalytic impairment, as the route by which missense alleles abolish activity.

evidence.snippet: PUS3 encodes the pseudouridylate synthase 3, an enzyme catalyzing the formation of tRNA pseudouridine, which plays a critical role in tRNA structure, function, and stability.
evidence.explanation: States the gene product's enzymatic role and why its loss matters for tRNA.

steps/2.description: PUS3 is a stand-alone, guide-RNA-independent pseudouridine synthase of the TruA/Pus3 family that isomerises uridine to pseudouridine in the anticodon stem loop of cytosolic tRNAs. Cryo-EM shows it acts as a symmetric homodimer that clamps the tRNA and presents the target uridine to its active site. Two distinct routes destroy that activity in patients: outright absence of the protein from truncating alleles, and post-translational depletion from missense alleles that impair thermostability (p.Tyr71Cys) or promote aggregation (p.Ile299Thr).

evidence.snippet: Since tRNAPhe from LCLs with the Arg435* allele of PUS3 had almost exactly 1 mole/mole less Ψ than control LCLs, we infer that the Arg435* allele nearly completely knocks out PUS3 function due to truncation of the conserved domain and the last 45 amino acids
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the stoichiometric loss of one pseudouridine per tRNA molecule in patient cells.

evidence.snippet: By contrast, the levels of the other modifications of tRNAPhe (Cm, Gm, m2G, m1A, m7G, and m5C) were all very similar in all of the LCLs including WT
evidence.explanation: Shows the deficit is specific to the PUS3-dependent modification, excluding a generalised tRNA-modification failure.

evidence.snippet: our results directly illustrate the link between the identified PUS3 variants and reduced Ψ levels in the patient cells, providing a molecular explanation for the observed clinical phenotypes.
evidence.explanation: Independent replication in a second patient set and with a different allele class, closing the loop from genotype to reduced pseudouridine.

steps/3.description: Pseudouridine at positions 38 and 39 sits in the anticodon stem loop, the part of the tRNA that pairs with the codon. Its extra imino group provides additional hydrogen bonding and rigidifies the loop, so its absence is expected to destabilise anticodon stem loop architecture. In the founding family the deficit was quantified as almost exactly one missing mole of pseudouridine per mole of tRNA-Phe, while every other measured modification of the same tRNA was unchanged, establishing that the lesion is specific to the PUS3 site rather than a general collapse of tRNA modification.

evidence.snippet: Bacterial truA mutants have significant growth defects (Chang et al. 1971; Tsui et al. 1991), while S. cerevisiae pus3Δ mutants are slow growing and temperature-sensitive
evidence.explanation: Orthologue evidence that loss of this specific pseudouridylation is physiologically consequential; tagged MODEL_ORGANISM because it is bacterial and yeast data, not human.

evidence.snippet: Our work provides the molecular basis for PUS3-mediated tRNA modification in humans and explains how its tRNA modification activity is linked to intellectual disabilities.
evidence.explanation: The structural study frames the disease link as running specifically through the tRNA modification activity. Its negative mRNA-substrate result does not test impaired translation through tRNA hypomodification.

steps/4.description: Reduced anticodon-loop pseudouridylation is expected to degrade the accuracy and efficiency of protein synthesis. In lower organisms loss of the orthologous enzyme is clearly consequential: bacterial truA mutants grow poorly and yeast pus3-delta mutants are slow-growing and temperature-sensitive with reduced frameshifting fidelity. The corresponding measurement has not been made in human patient neurons.

evidence.snippet: The phenotype we observe in the context of PUS3 deficiency is largely brain-specific.
evidence.explanation: States the brain-predominant character of the clinical endpoint.

evidence.snippet: Our finding adds to a growing list of intellectual disability disorders that are caused by perturbation of various tRNA modifications, which highlights the sensitivity of the brain to these highly conserved processes.
evidence.explanation: Places the disorder within the wider class of tRNA-modification intellectual disability disorders.

evidence.snippet: The clinical picture was dominated by global developmental delay, epilepsy, hypotonia and microcephaly.
evidence.explanation: Defines the composition of the neurodevelopmental endpoint across the largest pooled cohort.

steps/5.description: The clinical endpoint. Despite wide tissue expression of PUS3, the phenotype is largely brain-predominant: global developmental delay, severe to profound intellectual disability, poor or absent speech, hypotonia, epilepsy, microcephaly and variable structural or white-matter brain abnormalities. Growth failure, pigmentary and ocular features accompany the neurological core in a subset. This places PUS3 alongside ADAT3, WDR4, NSUN2 and FTSJ1 in the family of tRNA-modification intellectual disability disorders.

evidence.snippet: there was evidence of dysgenesis of corpus callosum, mild diffuse brain atrophy and a prominent cisterna magna

evidence.snippet: We identified a novel homozygous PUS3 frameshift variant in a child with facial dysmorphisms, growth failure, microcephaly, retinal dystrophy, cerebellar hypoplasia, congenital heart defect, and right kidney hypoplasia.

steps/14.description: Speech is poor or absent in every individual for whom it has been assessed, and is disproportionately affected even against the background of global developmental delay. One child spoke first single words only at age eight.

steps/15.description: Gross and fine motor milestones are delayed, and many individuals never achieve independent ambulation or achieve it only with assistance. Motor delay is closely tied to the generalised hypotonia and is part of the global developmental delay rather than a separable regression.

steps/16.description: Behavioural disturbance is common and heterogeneous, reported as anxiety, attention disorder or aggression; autistic features have been noted in a subset of those formally assessed. There is no single characteristic behavioural signature, which distinguishes this disorder from the very-early-onset aggression that characterises PUS7 deficiency.

evidence.snippet: we observe that the PUS3 protein levels as well as the level of PUS3-dependent Ψ levels are strongly reduced in fibroblasts derived from all three patients.
evidence.explanation: Directly links patient PUS3 alleles to depletion of the enzyme and of its catalytic product in patient-derived cells.

edges/1.description: Truncating alleles remove the enzyme outright, while the studied missense alleles deplete it post-translationally, so both arms of the allelic spectrum converge on loss of available PUS3 activity in the cell.

evidence.snippet: Consistent with the known role of Pus3 in isomerizing uracil to pseudouridine at positions 38 and 39 in tRNA, we found a significant reduction in this post-transcriptional modification of tRNA in patient cells.
evidence.explanation: Measures the loss of the specific modification directly in patient-derived cells carrying the disease allele.

edges/2.description: Loss of the only enzyme that installs pseudouridine at these two positions leaves the corresponding uridines unmodified in patient tRNA.

evidence.snippet: PUS3 encodes a transfer RNA (tRNA) pseudouridine synthase essential for translational fidelity.
evidence.explanation: States the accepted functional role of the enzyme in translational fidelity. Indirect because the statement is a background assertion rather than a measurement of translation in patient cells.

evidence.snippet: it is possible that brain-specific phenotype reflects a higher sensitivity to reduced translational efficiency by the brain compared to other organs

evidence.snippet: The clinical picture was dominated by global developmental delay, epilepsy, hypotonia and microcephaly.

edges/5.description: Summary manifestation edge. Global developmental delay from infancy is the presenting clinical expression of the disturbed brain development this endpoint node describes, named first among the dominant features of the pooled cohort.

edges/6.description: Summary manifestation edge. Severe to profound intellectual disability is the cognitive expression of the endpoint and the feature on which the founding family was ascertained.

edges/7.description: Summary manifestation edge. Expressive language is disproportionately affected within the global delay, poor or absent in every individual assessed for it.

edges/8.description: Summary manifestation edge. Delayed gross and fine motor milestones are the motor expression of the endpoint, tightly interwoven with the generalised hypotonia.

evidence.snippet: The clinical picture was dominated by global developmental delay, epilepsy, hypotonia and microcephaly.
evidence.explanation: Documents this feature within the PUS3 neurodevelopmental phenotype. It supports the clinical manifestation link, but does not demonstrate its causal mechanism or identify the intervening cells and pathways.

edges/9.description: Summary manifestation edge. Axial and appendicular hypotonia from infancy is among the dominant features of the pooled cohort. A central contribution is plausible, but the neural circuitry or other tissue contribution to reduced tone has not been established in PUS3 deficiency.

evidence.snippet: The clinical picture was dominated by global developmental delay, epilepsy, hypotonia and microcephaly.
evidence.explanation: Documents this feature within the PUS3 neurodevelopmental phenotype. It supports the clinical manifestation link, but does not demonstrate its causal mechanism or identify the intervening cells and pathways.

edges/10.description: Summary manifestation edge. Epilepsy of heterogeneous semiology affects most individuals and is among the dominant features of the pooled cohort; the specific route from disturbed brain development to cortical hyperexcitability has not been dissected in this disorder.

evidence.snippet: The clinical picture was dominated by global developmental delay, epilepsy, hypotonia and microcephaly.
evidence.explanation: Documents this feature within the PUS3 neurodevelopmental phenotype. It supports the clinical manifestation link, but does not demonstrate its causal mechanism or identify the intervening cells and pathways.

edges/11.description: Summary manifestation edge. Postnatal microcephaly - normal birth head circumference with later deceleration in the founding sisters - is the head growth signature of the impaired brain development this node describes.

edges/12.description: Summary manifestation edge. The stable, nonprogressive subcortical white matter signal change is a neuroimaging correlate of the developmental brain disorder. Stability in the reported adolescent is compatible with a developmental lesion, but does not establish the cellular mechanism of the white matter abnormalities or a direct causal link.

edges/13.description: Summary manifestation edge. Callosal dysgenesis, documented in one founding sister and explicitly absent in other affected individuals, belongs to the variable structural spectrum of the abnormal brain development.

edges/14.description: Summary manifestation edge. Cerebellar hypoplasia, reported once at the severe end of the spectrum, is a developmental brain malformation within the same variable structural spectrum.

edges/15.description: Summary manifestation edge. Heterogeneous behavioural disturbance, including autistic features in a subset of those formally assessed, is a recognised expression of severe neurodevelopmental impairment; no single behavioural signature exists, and the intervening circuit mechanisms remain unknown.

evidence.snippet: Biallelic variants in PUS3 have recently been recognized as a rare cause of neurodevelopmental disorders. Pseudouridine synthase-3 encoded by PUS3 is an enzyme important for modification of various RNAs, including transfer RNA (tRNA).
evidence.explanation: Establishes PUS3 as a recognised Mendelian disease gene and names its gene product and substrate class.

evidence.snippet: Our findings provide additional evidence to establish loss of PUS3 function as a cause of intellectual disability.
evidence.explanation: Independent replication in a second consanguineous population, cited by OMIM as one of the two summary sources for the disease entry.

evidence.snippet: Genomic mutations in the human pseudouridine synthase 3 gene (PUS3) have been identified in patients with neurodevelopmental disorders.
evidence.explanation: Confirms the gene-disease relationship from an independent group.

genes/0.notes:
PUS3 (11q24.2, gene MIM 616283) encodes a 481-amino-acid, guide-RNA-independent pseudouridine synthase of the TruA/Pus3 family that isomerises uridine to pseudouridine at positions 38 and 39 of the tRNA anticodon stem loop. The orthologous enzyme acts at U38/U39/U40 in bacteria (TruA), at U38 and U39 in S. cerevisiae, and preferentially at U39 in mouse. The reference transcript used in the clinical literature is NM_031307.
Gene identity was verified against the MONDO gene-association relation (`RO:0004003 HGNC:25461 ! PUS3`) and against the HGNC record `hgnc:25461`, whose definition "pseudouridine synthase 3" cites PMID:27055666. This is deliberately distinct from the family members PUS1 (hgnc:15508), which causes myopathy with lactic acidosis and sideroblastic anaemia, and PUS7 (hgnc:26033), which causes a separate intellectual disability syndrome already curated in this knowledge base; see differential_diagnoses. Note also that MIM 616283 is the PUS3 GENE entry whereas MIM 617051 is the DISEASE entry that MONDO:0014886 cross-references.
Reported allelic spectrum comprises roughly 17 distinct variants across the published cohort: eight missense, seven protein-truncating (three nonsense, two single-base deletions, two single-base duplications), one splice-region variant and one initiation-codon substitution. Both homozygous and compound heterozygous genotypes occur in approximately equal numbers.

evidence.snippet: There is a history of seizures at 10 months of age but she has been seizure-free on multiple antiepileptic medications.
evidence.explanation: Documents antiepileptic medication achieving seizure freedom in an affected individual.

treatments/0.description: Epilepsy is managed with standard antiseizure medication chosen by seizure type. There is no PUS3-specific drug recommendation and no evidence favouring one agent; response is variable, with some individuals achieving seizure freedom on multiple agents and others retaining breakthrough seizures.

evidence.snippet: The clinical picture was dominated by global developmental delay, epilepsy, hypotonia and microcephaly.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the developmental and motor targets of rehabilitation. Indirect because the cohort study characterises the deficits rather than evaluating any rehabilitative intervention; no trial evidence for efficacy exists in this disorder.

treatments/1.description: Management is entirely supportive. Early and sustained physical, occupational and speech or augmentative-communication therapy addresses the hypotonia, motor delay and severely limited expressive language that dominate function, and physiotherapy plus orthopaedic surveillance addresses the scoliosis and contracture risk that follow from hypotonia and limited mobility.

evidence.snippet: She has coarse facial features, bilateral strabismus, grey sclera and extensive Mongolian spots
evidence.explanation: Documents the ocular findings that make ophthalmological surveillance appropriate. Indirect because the paper reports the findings but does not evaluate a surveillance or treatment programme.

evidence.snippet: We identified a novel homozygous PUS3 frameshift variant in a child with facial dysmorphisms, growth failure, microcephaly, retinal dystrophy, cerebellar hypoplasia, congenital heart defect, and right kidney hypoplasia.
evidence.explanation: Documents retinal dystrophy, the finding that makes formal retinal assessment rather than a simple squint check appropriate. Indirect because it is a single case observation, not an evaluated protocol.

treatments/2.description: Baseline and periodic ophthalmological review is warranted because strabismus is common, grey sclerae are part of the diagnostic picture, and retinal dystrophy, nystagmus, optic disc pallor and abnormal visual fixation have each been reported. Untreated strabismus in a child with severe developmental delay risks amblyopia that further limits an already constrained visual and communicative repertoire. Scoped and named as surveillance to match its NCIT action term: the entry asserts case detection through formal eye examination, not any specific corrective intervention, because no strabismus or retinal treatment outcome has been reported in this disorder.

evidence.snippet: We describe a 17-year-old girl born to second-degree consanguineous parents presenting with lifelong global developmental delay, microcephaly, gray sclera, dysmorphic features, and intellectual disability.
evidence.explanation: Documents the consanguineous family structure in which recurrence-risk counselling and carrier testing are most consequential.

treatments/3.description: Once the biallelic PUS3 genotype is established, counselling covers the 25 percent sibling recurrence risk, carrier testing of at-risk relatives, and the availability of prenatal diagnosis and preimplantation genetic testing. This is the only intervention with a preventive rather than symptomatic role, and it is particularly relevant because many reported families are consanguineous.

evidence.snippet: Her stable neurological course into late adolescence broadens the phenotypic spectrum of PUS3 deficiency and underscores the need for long-term clinical monitoring in disorders of tRNA modification.
evidence.explanation: An explicit recommendation for long-term clinical monitoring in this disorder.

treatments/4.description: Because the natural history extends into adulthood and the white matter changes are stable rather than progressive, periodic rather than intensive neurological review is appropriate, with attention to emerging or evolving seizures, scoliosis and functional decline. The 2026 report makes this recommendation explicitly.

evidence.snippet: Further functional studies are necessary to understand involvement of PUS3 and tRNA biogenesis in normal and abnormal brain development.
evidence.explanation: The largest cohort study states explicitly that the mechanistic link from PUS3 to brain development remains unresolved.

open_questions/0.rationale: This is the weakest link in the causal chain. Every step from the PUS3 genotype to depleted pseudouridine at positions 38 and 39 has been measured directly in patient cells by two independent groups. The step from there to impaired translation is inferred from tRNA structural chemistry and from bacterial truA and yeast pus3 orthologue phenotypes, and the step from impaired translation to selective vulnerability of the developing brain is inferred from the pattern shared across the tRNA-modification intellectual disability disorders. No ribosome profiling, proteomics or reporter-fidelity measurement has been reported in a human PUS3-deficient neural cell. Until that measurement exists, the mechanistic explanation for why a housekeeping tRNA modification produces a brain-predominant phenotype remains a hypothesis rather than a finding.

evidence.snippet: Gray sclera, which has previously been suggested to be a characteristic feature of PUS3-associated phenotypes, was reported in only seven individuals.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates the precedent: a pigmentary feature considered characteristic from early reports deflated to a minority finding once a real cohort was assembled, which is the concern raised for dermal melanocytosis.

evidence.snippet: She has coarse facial features, bilateral strabismus, grey sclera and extensive Mongolian spots
evidence.explanation: The single-family observation on which the whole Orphanet label rests, and therefore the observation whose generalisability is in question.

open_questions/1.rationale: Extensive Mongolian spots appear in all three sisters of the founding Saudi family and are prominent enough to have named the disorder in Orphanet and MONDO. Yet the feature is absent from the abstract of the 21-individual pooled cohort, which enumerates gray sclera among pigmentary findings but not dermal melanocytosis, and it is not mentioned in the Italian, Polish or Turkish reports. Congenital dermal melanocytosis is also common in the general population of several ancestries, including the one the founding family belongs to, which makes a coincidental co-occurrence within one consanguineous sibship entirely plausible. Two things hinge on the answer. If the association is real, then PUS3 loss must perturb dermal melanocyte migration or retention and the pathograph is missing a node. If it is not, the MONDO label is actively misleading and steers curators and clinicians towards the lysosomal storage disorders. Grey sclerae, which is plausibly the ocular counterpart of the same melanocytic process, went from "characteristic" to 7/21 once a real cohort was assembled - the same deflation may await dermal melanocytosis.

evidence.snippet: This patient further expands the phenotypic spectrum of PUS3-related disorders to include a more severe syndromic presentation.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the expanded syndromic phenotype motivating this question. The quote does not itself establish the absence of a mechanism; the mechanistic gap is the curation assessment recorded in the rationale.

open_questions/2.rationale: The pathograph explains the brain-predominant core of the disorder through the tRNA hypomodification chain, and the terminal node carries manifestation edges only for the neurological features. The somatic features are deliberately left unwired. The founding paper's own proposal - that the brain is simply the tissue most sensitive to reduced translational efficiency - predicts a brain-limited phenotype and therefore does not account for growth failure, coarse facies, strabismus, grey sclerae, retinal dystrophy, renal hypoplasia, a congenital heart defect or scoliosis, and no published study has connected any of these features to the tRNA defect. For scoliosis specifically it is additionally unresolved whether it is a primary skeletal feature at all or secondary to hypotonia and limited mobility, which would route it through the neurological arm. Wiring these phenotypes into the pathograph now would manufacture edges the literature cannot support; the honest representation is this recorded gap. The related but distinct question of whether extensive dermal melanocytosis is a disease feature at all is tracked separately in pus3_dermal_melanocytosis_generalisability.

evidence.snippet: the intracellular stress hub formed by the synergistic action of oxidative stress (OS) and endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS) serves as the initiating factor
evidence.explanation: Establishes OS and ERS synergy as the initiating hub driving granulosa cell dysfunction and autophagy-ferroptosis crosstalk in PCOS.

steps/7.description: Synergistic oxidative stress (OS) and endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS) form an intracellular stress hub that initiates autophagy-ferroptosis crosstalk in ovarian granulosa cells, driving follicular atresia and ovulatory dysfunction.

evidence.snippet: circadian rhythm disruption and epigenetic reprogramming, respectively, cement this imbalance at the temporal and molecular memory levels.
evidence.explanation: Highlights circadian rhythm disruption and epigenetic reprogramming as the mechanisms that entrench the ferroptosis-autophagy imbalance in PCOS.

steps/8.description: Circadian rhythm disruption and epigenetic reprogramming entrench the granulosa cell autophagy-ferroptosis imbalance at the temporal and molecular memory levels, amplifying follicular atresia.

evidence.snippet: The dysfunction of GCs in PCOS is not an isolated event involving a single mode of cell death, but rather a pathological crosstalk arising from the disruption of the dynamic equilibrium between autophagy and ferroptosis.
evidence.explanation: The review identifies ferroptosis-autophagy crosstalk as a central feature of granulosa-cell dysfunction in PCOS.

evidence.snippet: selective autophagy (e.g., ferritinophagy and mitophagy) acts as a key amplifier of ferroptosis by exacerbating iron overload and energy collapse.
evidence.explanation: Supports selective autophagy as an amplifier of ferroptosis through iron overload and energetic failure.

steps/9.description: Granulosa cell dysfunction in PCOS arises from pathological crosstalk between autophagy and ferroptosis rather than from a single mode of cell death. Selective autophagy mechanisms (ferritinophagy and mitophagy) amplify ferroptosis through iron overload and energy collapse, driving follicular atresia and ovulatory dysfunction.

evidence.snippet: elevated PCSK9 levels induce lipid metabolism abnormalities in PCOS mice, subsequently activating AMP-activated protein kinase and glycogen synthase kinase 3β within follicles. This activation triggers granulosa cell apoptosis
evidence.explanation: Direct mechanistic evidence in PCOS model mice establishing the PCSK9 → lipid abnormality → AMPK/GSK-3β → apoptosis cascade as a driver of granulosa cell death.

evidence.snippet: Granulosa cell apoptosis in the ovaries is one of the primary factors affecting follicular growth and development as well as oocyte maturation in PCOS, yet its pathological mechanisms remain unclear.
evidence.explanation: Establishes granulosa cell apoptosis as a primary mechanism impairing follicular development and oocyte maturation in PCOS, motivating mechanistic investigation of upstream drivers like PCSK9.

steps/10.description: Elevated PCSK9 (proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type-9) in ovarian follicles triggers lipid metabolism abnormalities that activate AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and glycogen synthase kinase 3β (GSK-3β), leading to granulosa cell apoptosis. This PCSK9-lipid-AMPK/GSK-3β cascade represents a distinct apoptotic pathway in granulosa cell death, independent of the ferroptosis-autophagy crosstalk mechanism, and may contribute to follicular atresia and ovulatory dysfunction in PCOS.

evidence.snippet: the gut-ovarian axis's long-range amplification effect, mediated by gut microbiome (GM) dysregulation and low-grade chronic inflammation (LGI), collectively disrupting cellular homeostasis
evidence.explanation: Establishes the gut-ovarian axis as a long-range amplification mechanism linking microbiome dysregulation to granulosa cell dysfunction via chronic inflammation.

steps/11.description: Dysbiosis-driven gut microbiome dysfunction amplifies low-grade chronic inflammation via the gut-ovarian axis, exacerbating granulosa cell dysfunction and follicular atresia through long-range immune and metabolic signaling.

evidence.snippet: Notably, our analyses reveal a predominant enrichment of metabolic dysregulation-associated pathways in East Asian PCOS, whereas European PCOS exhibits a stronger inflammatory and immune-related signature.
evidence.explanation: Population-stratified gene prioritization reveals distinct metabolic versus inflammatory molecular signatures across East Asian and European populations, supported by transcriptomic validation in PCOS patient samples.

evidence.snippet: genes like INS, INSR and IGF1R implicating insulin signaling and FSHR, LHCGR involving gonadotropin related signaling were exclusively present in the EAS population
evidence.explanation: East Asian PCOS prioritizes insulin/IGF and gonadotropin signaling genes, reflecting the metabolic and hormonal dysfunction-dominant phenotype in this population.

evidence.snippet: immune-related genes were differentially prioritized in the EUR population (Supplementary Data 2, II) with, NF-B1, APP, IRF1 and few others
evidence.explanation: European PCOS shows preferential prioritization of immune-centric genes, reflecting the stronger inflammatory and immune-related signature of this population.

steps/12.description: PCOS manifests with distinct molecular pathophysiology across populations. East Asian PCOS exhibits predominant enrichment of metabolic dysregulation pathways with emphasis on insulin/IGF signaling and gonadotropin receptor pathways. European PCOS shows a stronger inflammatory and immune-related signature, featuring enrichment of the TLR4-NF-κB-NLRP3 signaling axis. This population-specific molecular heterogeneity suggests distinct pathophysiological drivers and therapeutic opportunities across ancestries.

evidence.snippet: Compelling evidence suggests that hyperandrogenism is not just a primary feature of PCOS. Instead, it may be a causative factor for this condition.
evidence.explanation: This review establishes hyperandrogenism as potentially causative rather than merely symptomatic in PCOS pathophysiology.

evidence.snippet: LHCGR and 17α-hydroxylase/17-20-lyase (CYP17A1) protein levels are increased in polycystic ovaries (PCOs).
evidence.explanation: Direct evidence of increased androgen biosynthetic machinery (CYP17A1) in PCOS ovaries, supporting intrinsic theca cell abnormality.

evidence.snippet: A significant increase in the intensity of immunostaining for CYP17A1 was identified in antral follicles in sections of PCO compared with ovaries from normal women (P = 0.04).
evidence.explanation: Quantitative demonstration of elevated CYP17A1 protein in polycystic ovaries compared to controls.

evidence.snippet: A higher proportion of theca cells from anovulatory PCO expressed LHCGR protein when compared with control ovaries (P = 0.01).
evidence.explanation: Increased LH receptor expression in theca cells explains heightened LH-driven androgen production in PCOS.

steps/13.description: Excess androgen production from ovarian theca cells and adrenal glands leads to hirsutism, acne, and alopecia. Elevated LH stimulates theca cell androgen production.

evidence.snippet: The majority of patients have elevated LH levels in plasma and a persistent rapid frequency of LH (GnRH) pulse secretion, the mechanisms of which are unclear.
evidence.explanation: Human endocrine profiling supports elevated LH and rapid LH/GnRH pulse secretion as a PCOS pathophysiology node.

evidence.snippet: These results suggest that although the elevated LH pulse frequency in PCOS may in part reflect impaired sensitivity to E2 and P, continuing actions of hyperandrogenemia are important for sustaining the abnormal hypothalamic sensitivity to feedback inhibition by ovarian steroids.
evidence.explanation: Antiandrogen intervention restoring feedback sensitivity supports a bidirectional link between hyperandrogenism and hypothalamic-pituitary dysregulation.

steps/14.description: Impaired hypothalamic-pituitary sensitivity to estradiol and progesterone negative feedback maintains rapid LH/GnRH pulse secretion. Elevated LH then stimulates theca-cell androgen biosynthesis, while hyperandrogenism can sustain the abnormal feedback state.

evidence.snippet: Because insulin binding was not changed, we conclude that the major lesion causing insulin resistance in PCO is a striking decrease in insulin sensitivity secondary to a defect in the insulin receptor and/or postreceptor signal transduction.
evidence.explanation: Human clamp and adipocyte data support a post-binding/post-receptor insulin signaling defect as an intrinsic PCOS mechanism.

evidence.snippet: We conclude that there is a physiologically relevant defect in insulin receptor signaling in PCOS that is independent of obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
evidence.explanation: Skeletal muscle signaling data support an obesity-independent insulin receptor signaling defect in PCOS.

evidence.snippet: There is a post-binding defect in receptor signaling likely due to increased receptor and insulin receptor substrate-1 serine phosphorylation that selectively affects metabolic but not mitogenic pathways in classic insulin target tissues and in the ovary.
evidence.explanation: Review evidence supports selective metabolic insulin resistance with preserved non-metabolic insulin signaling branches.

evidence.snippet: Hyperinsulinemia (i.e., elevated insulin without hypoglycemia) is a common metabolic feature of PCOS that worsens its reproductive symptoms by exacerbating pituitary hormone imbalances and increasing levels of bioactive androgens.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates the direct mechanistic link between hyperinsulinemia and worsening of reproductive and androgenic features in PCOS.

evidence.snippet: However, it is challenging to define the sequential relationship between insulin sensitivity and insulin secretion, as they are tightly interlinked, and evidence suggests that hyperinsulinemia can alternatively precede insulin resistance.
evidence.explanation: Challenges traditional causality and suggests hyperinsulinemia may be primary rather than compensatory in some PCOS cases.

evidence.snippet: Notably, other drivers of hyperinsulinemia (outside of insulin resistance) may be highly relevant in the context of PCOS. For instance, high androgen levels can augment both hyperinsulinemia and insulin resistance, generating a self-perpetuating cycle of reproductive and metabolic dysfunction.
evidence.explanation: Describes the vicious cycle where androgens exacerbate both hyperinsulinemia and insulin resistance in PCOS.

steps/15.description: PCOS-associated insulin resistance can reflect an intrinsic post-binding or post-receptor defect in insulin signaling that is independent of obesity. Defective insulin receptor or IRS-associated signaling decreases metabolic glucose disposal while ovarian steroidogenic actions of insulin may remain active, allowing insulin and LH to amplify androgen production.

evidence.snippet: Obesity, particularly the abdominal phenotype, may be partly responsible for insulin resistance and associated hyperinsulinemia in women with PCOS.
evidence.explanation: Supports a distinct adiposity-amplified insulin resistance node for obese PCOS.

evidence.snippet: Therefore, obesity-related hyperinsulinemia may play a key role in favouring hyperandrogenism in these women.
evidence.explanation: Supports the adiposity-to-hyperinsulinemia-to-hyperandrogenism causal route.

evidence.snippet: This disease causes menstrual, metabolic, and biochemical abnormalities such as hyperandrogenism, oligo-anovulatory menstrual cycles, polycystic ovary, hyperleptinemia, insulin resistance (IR), and cardiometabolic disorders, often associated with overweight or obesity and visceral adiposity.
evidence.explanation: Recent review evidence supports separating visceral-adiposity-associated PCOS metabolic dysfunction from nonobese mechanisms.

steps/16.description: Abdominal or visceral adiposity amplifies insulin resistance and hyperinsulinemia in susceptible PCOS patients. This pathway separates obesity-related hepatic/adipose insulin resistance from intrinsic lean-PCOS insulin signaling defects and explains why obesity worsens androgenic and reproductive features without being required for PCOS.

evidence.snippet: Because PCOS is associated with a 2- to 3-fold increase in growing FN, we investigated whether an increased AMH serum level correlates to other hormonal and/or U/S features of PCOS.
evidence.explanation: Documents the 2-3 fold increase in small growing follicle number characteristic of PCOS polycystic morphology.

evidence.snippet: Mean serum AMH level was markedly increased in the PCOS group (47.1 +/- 22.9 vs. 20.8 +/- 11.6 pmol/liter in controls; P < 0.0001), an increase in the same order of magnitude as the one of the FN in the 2- to 5-mm range at U/S (12.8 +/- 8.3 vs. 4.8 +/- 1.9; P < 0.0001, respectively).
evidence.explanation: Shows parallel elevation of AMH levels and small antral follicle count in PCOS, implicating AMH in follicular arrest.

evidence.snippet: We hypothesize that an increased AMH tone within the cohort could be involved in the follicular arrest of PCOS, by interacting negatively with FSH at the time of selection.
evidence.explanation: Proposes mechanism by which elevated AMH interferes with FSH action to prevent dominant follicle selection in PCOS.

steps/17.description: Disrupted folliculogenesis with arrest at small antral stage leads to anovulation. Multiple small follicles accumulate (polycystic morphology) without dominant follicle selection.

evidence.snippet: Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) is related to pro-apoptotic and pro-inflammatory conditions generated by Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the link between ER stress, inflammation, and apoptotic pathways in PCOS pathophysiology.

evidence.snippet: The levels of TNF-α (p = 0.009), IL-18 (p = 0.003), IL-6 (p = 0.013) and active caspase-3 (p = 0.012) were also statistically significant lower in the therapy group.
evidence.explanation: Shows that TNF-alpha, IL-18 and IL-6 are pharmacologically reducible in women with PCOS, indicating an active inflammatory state that is a treatment target. It compares treated vs placebo PCOS arms, so it does NOT by itself demonstrate that these cytokines are elevated in PCOS relative to healthy controls; a PCOS-versus-control comparison is still needed for the "elevated inflammatory markers" claim.

steps/18.description: Elevated inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-6) contribute to insulin resistance and cardiovascular risk in PCOS.

edges/7.description: Androgen excess can worsen insulin resistance and hyperinsulinemia, creating a self-perpetuating endocrine-metabolic loop.

edges/8.description: Hyperandrogenism favors visceral adiposity and adverse adipose signaling, which can amplify insulin resistance in obese PCOS.

edges/9.description: Ongoing androgen excess helps sustain abnormal hypothalamic sensitivity to estradiol/progesterone negative feedback, maintaining rapid LH/GnRH pulse secretion.

edges/10.description: Elevated androgen exposure disrupts follicle maturation and contributes to anovulation.

edges/11.description: Rapid LH/GnRH pulse secretion increases LH action on ovarian theca cells, promoting androgen biosynthesis.

edges/12.description: Hyperinsulinemia arising from impaired insulin signaling can act as a co-gonadotropin and increase bioactive androgen exposure.

edges/13.description: Hyperinsulinemia and androgen amplification contribute to follicular arrest and anovulation.

edges/14.description: Obesity-related hyperinsulinemia increases ovarian androgen synthesis and lowers SHBG, raising bioactive androgen exposure.

edges/15.description: Visceral adiposity and insulin resistance contribute to the inflammatory state shared by PCOS, obesity, type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular disease.

edges/16.description: Oxidative and ER stress serve as the initiating hub that triggers downstream autophagy-ferroptosis crosstalk in granulosa cells.

edges/17.description: Gut microbiome dysregulation amplifies systemic low-grade chronic inflammation via the gut-ovarian axis.

edges/18.description: Granulosa-cell ferroptosis and autophagy-amplified cell death promote follicular atresia and impair dominant-follicle selection.

edges/19.description: Circadian and epigenetic reprogramming entrench the autophagy-ferroptosis imbalance rather than initiating it.

edges/20.description: PCSK9-driven granulosa cell apoptosis leads to loss of granulosa cell support for follicular maturation, resulting in follicular arrest and anovulation.

evidence.snippet: The comparison of miR-130b-3p in normal and PCOS theca cells demonstrated decreased miR-130b-3p expression in PCOS theca cells, which was correlated with increased DENND1A.V2, cytochrome P450 17α-hydroxylase (CYP17A1) mRNA and androgen biosynthesis.
evidence.explanation: Connects the DENND1A risk locus to the intrinsic theca-cell steroidogenic phenotype curated under Hyperandrogenism: loss of miR-130b-3p repression raises DENND1A.V2 and CYP17A1 together with androgen output in theca cells isolated from women with PCOS. In vitro in isolated theca cells, and the DENND1A.V2 link is correlative within that system.

evidence.snippet: carriers of previously reported rare variants in DENND1A, a gene that regulates androgen biosynthesis, were significantly more likely to have the reproductive subtype of PCOS
evidence.explanation: Rare DENND1A variant carriers segregate with the reproductive (higher LH and SHBG, lower BMI and insulin) rather than the metabolic phenotype cluster, so this locus is not uniformly distributed across PCOS. European ancestry, NIH criteria, and a family-based classification cohort of 73.

genes/0.notes: Commonly prioritized in both East Asian and European populations through integrative gene prioritization combining regulatory genomics, long-range chromatin interactions, QTLs, and protein networks. The functional route to hyperandrogenism runs through the truncated DENND1A variant 2 isoform in theca cells rather than through the full-length gene product.

evidence.snippet: genes like INS, INSR and IGF1R implicating insulin signaling and FSHR, LHCGR involving gonadotropin related signaling were exclusively present in the EAS population
evidence.explanation: Gonadotropin-signaling gene exclusively prioritized in the East Asian PCOS gene-prioritization list.

genes/2.notes: Gonadotropin signaling gene; prioritized in East Asian PCOS (rank 13) more highly than European populations (rank 53), reflecting enhanced LH-driven ovarian androgen production in metabolic-dominant phenotypes.

evidence.snippet: genes like INS, INSR and IGF1R implicating insulin signaling and FSHR, LHCGR involving gonadotropin related signaling were exclusively present in the EAS population
evidence.explanation: Gonadotropin-signaling gene exclusively prioritized in the East Asian PCOS gene-prioritization list.

genes/3.notes: Follicle-stimulating hormone receptor; prioritized in both populations (East Asian rank 6, European rank 58), reflects gonadotropin dysregulation as a shared PCOS mechanism with population-specific emphasis.

evidence.snippet: genes like INS, INSR and IGF1R implicating insulin signaling and FSHR, LHCGR involving gonadotropin related signaling were exclusively present in the EAS population
evidence.explanation: Insulin-signaling gene exclusively prioritized in the East Asian PCOS gene-prioritization list.

genes/4.notes: Insulin; exclusively prioritized in top 50 genes of East Asian PCOS, reflecting enrichment of insulin signaling and metabolic dysregulation pathways in East Asian populations.

evidence.snippet: genes like INS, INSR and IGF1R implicating insulin signaling and FSHR, LHCGR involving gonadotropin related signaling were exclusively present in the EAS population
evidence.explanation: Insulin-receptor gene exclusively prioritized in the East Asian PCOS gene-prioritization list.

genes/5.notes: Insulin receptor; exclusively prioritized in top 50 genes of East Asian PCOS, supporting insulin resistance as a primary metabolic driver in East Asian populations.

evidence.snippet: genes like INS, INSR and IGF1R implicating insulin signaling and FSHR, LHCGR involving gonadotropin related signaling were exclusively present in the EAS population
evidence.explanation: IGF-signaling gene prioritized in the East Asian PCOS gene-prioritization list.

genes/6.notes: Insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor; prioritized in East Asian PCOS, part of metabolic pathway signature; interacts with ERBB3 and other growth factor receptors.

genes/7.notes: Receptor tyrosine kinase; top prioritized core gene in both populations; central hub in metabolic-dominant (East Asian) and inflammatory-dominant (European) PCOS networks; interacts with IGF1R, EGFR, and GRB2.

genes/8.notes: Epidermal growth factor receptor; commonly prioritized in both populations; exclusively enriched in growth factor (EGFR/PDGFRA/FGFR) pathways in East Asian PCOS and connected to NF-κB inflammatory axis in European PCOS.

genes/9.notes: Yes-associated protein 1; prioritized in both populations, involved in Hippo signaling dysregulation implicated in PCOS follicular dysfunction.

genes/10.notes: Platelet-derived growth factor receptor alpha; enriched in the East Asian PCOS growth-factor signaling cascade (with EGFR and the FGFR receptor family) that is critical for follicular growth and ovulation. The paper's generic "FGFR" growth-factor enrichment (no single HGNC member specified) is captured here rather than as a separate non-specific gene entry.

evidence.snippet: immune-related genes were differentially prioritized in the EUR population (Supplementary Data 2, II) with, NF-B1, APP, IRF1 and few others
evidence.explanation: Immune/inflammatory gene preferentially prioritized in the European PCOS gene-prioritization list.

genes/11.notes: Amyloid precursor protein; immune/inflammatory gene preferentially prioritized in European PCOS; links oxidative stress and chronic inflammation to PCOS pathology.

evidence.explanation: NF-kB (NF-B1) immune-pathway gene preferentially prioritized in the European PCOS gene-prioritization list.

genes/12.notes: Nuclear factor kappa-B subunit 1; key inflammasome and immune pathway gene preferentially prioritized in European PCOS; reflects stronger chronic low-grade inflammatory signature.

evidence.snippet: immune-related genes were differentially prioritized in the EUR population (Supplementary Data 2, II) with, NF-B1, APP, IRF1 and few others
evidence.explanation: Interferon regulatory factor 1 immune-related gene preferentially prioritized in the European PCOS gene-prioritization list.

genes/13.notes: Interferon regulatory factor 1; immune-related gene preferentially prioritized in European PCOS; contributes to innate immune pathway dysregulation in inflammation-dominant phenotypes.

evidence.snippet: Polymorphisms in genes such as the androgen receptor (AR), cytochrome P450 17A1 (CYP17), and follicle-stimulating hormone receptor (FSHR) have been associated with altered steroidogenesis and ovarian dysfunction, thereby influencing disease severity.
evidence.explanation: Recent review establishes AR polymorphisms as contributors to altered steroidogenesis and ovarian dysfunction in PCOS pathophysiology.

genes/14.notes: Androgen receptor; polymorphisms in AR have been associated with altered steroidogenesis and ovarian dysfunction in PCOS. AR variants contribute to hyperandrogenism and ovarian androgen production.

evidence.snippet: Polymorphisms in genes such as the androgen receptor (AR), cytochrome P450 17A1 (CYP17), and follicle-stimulating hormone receptor (FSHR) have been associated with altered steroidogenesis and ovarian dysfunction, thereby influencing disease severity.
evidence.explanation: Recent review identifies CYP17 polymorphisms as key contributors to altered steroidogenesis and ovarian androgen dysregulation in PCOS.

genes/15.notes: Cytochrome P450 17A1 (17-alpha-hydroxylase/17-20-lyase); polymorphisms in CYP17 influence androgen biosynthesis capacity in theca cells. Variants affect the conversion of pregnenolone and progesterone to their 17-hydroxylated intermediates, critical steps in androgen production.

treatments/0.description: First-line for menstrual irregularity and hyperandrogenism.

evidence.snippet: In women with PCOS, Metformin induces a prompt decrease in LH-stimulated T secretion after only several days of use. This action precedes the medication's effects on insulin sensitivity or weight loss.
evidence.explanation: Randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled crossover in 19 women with PCOS: two days of metformin already lowered LH-stimulated testosterone, which is the shortest-latency human evidence that metformin acts on ovarian steroidogenesis directly and not only through insulin sensitisation. Small and short, and the free-androgen-index effect was only borderline.

treatments/1.description: Improves insulin sensitivity and may restore ovulation.

treatments/2.description: Anti-androgen for hirsutism and acne.

treatments/3.description: First-line ovulation induction for fertility.

treatments/5.description: Weight loss improves all PCOS features.

evidence.snippet: EGFR, ERBB3, and YAP1 present in the network of both the population , are involved in signaling by receptor tyrosine kinases and Hippo which are known for their  role in PCOS
evidence.explanation: Gene prioritization in both East Asian and European populations identifies ERBB family members as highly ranked druggable targets with direct therapeutic potential.

treatments/6.description: ERBB3 and ERBB2 signaling are central nodes in both East Asian and European PCOS genetic networks. ERBB-family receptor tyrosine kinase inhibition is a computationally identified candidate population-agnostic target for disrupting tyrosine kinase signaling implicated in follicular dysfunction and inflammatory amplification. This is an in silico target prediction from gene prioritization and has not been clinically tested in PCOS; no specific inhibitor is nominated by the source.

evidence.snippet: signaling pathways involving EGFR, PDGFRA and FGFR which are exclusively enriched due to peripheral genes (Figure 2A (iv)) are within the top priority pathways in EAS population.
evidence.explanation: Exclusive prioritization of FGFR/EGFR/PDGFRA pathways in East Asian PCOS identifies these as population-specific therapeutic targets for metabolic-dysregulation-dominant disease.

treatments/7.description: FGFR, EGFR, and PDGFRA signaling pathways are preferentially enriched in East Asian PCOS and are implicated in follicular growth and ovulation. Inhibition of these growth factor receptors is a computationally identified population-specific candidate target for metabolic-dominant PCOS phenotypes. This is an in silico target prediction from gene prioritization and has not been clinically tested in PCOS; no specific inhibitor is nominated by the source.

evidence.snippet: the prioritization of the TLR4 -NF-κB-NLRP3 signaling axis in EUR population
evidence.explanation: Gene prioritization in European PCOS reveals preferential dysregulation of TLR4-NF-kB-NLRP3 inflammatory axis, identifying NF-kB and inflammasome inhibition as population-specific therapeutic strategies for immune-dominant disease.

treatments/8.description: European PCOS exhibits preferential enrichment of TLR4-NF-kB-NLRP3 signaling and inflammasome activation. NF-kB and NLRP3 inflammasome inhibition are computationally identified population-specific candidate targets for inflammatory-dominant PCOS phenotypes, addressing chronic low-grade inflammation driven by immune pathway dysregulation. This is an in silico target prediction from gene prioritization and has not been clinically tested in PCOS; no specific inhibitor is nominated by the source.

evidence.snippet: Preclinical studies demonstrate that MSCs and their derivatives modulate inflammation, restore ovarian structure, and improve metabolic parameters
evidence.explanation: Narrative review summarizing preclinical (predominantly animal-model) mesenchymal stem cell and exosome regenerative studies in PCOS. Investigational and not yet clinically validated in humans.

treatments/9.description: Investigational, preclinical regenerative and cell-based disease-modifying strategy for PCOS. Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and their secreted derivatives (including exosomes), together with gene-edited induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) platforms, are being explored to move beyond symptom-focused management toward mechanism-directed intervention. In preclinical models these approaches modulate ovarian inflammation, restore ovarian structure, and improve metabolic parameters, while iPSC-based models support patient-specific investigation of steroidogenic and metabolic abnormalities. Not clinically validated in PCOS; translational barriers include targeted delivery, off-target effects, and phenotypic heterogeneity.

evidence.snippet: novel therapeutic strategies have emerged, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), microRNA-based therapies, and interleukin-22 (IL-22)-mediated interventions, which show potential in targeting IR and metabolic dysfunction in PCOS.
evidence.explanation: Recent comprehensive review identifies GLP-1RAs as an emerging therapeutic strategy with demonstrated potential in addressing insulin resistance and metabolic dysfunction in PCOS. The cited sentence is the narrative review's own summary of an emerging therapeutic landscape rather than a result from a primary clinical study, so it is graded OTHER.

treatments/10.description: GLP-1 receptor agonists are emerging as potential therapeutic agents in PCOS, targeting insulin resistance and metabolic dysregulation. Beyond their glucose-lowering effects, GLP-1RAs may improve androgen metabolism and ovulatory function through weight loss and insulin sensitization, offering a multi-pathway intervention approach in metabolic-dominant PCOS phenotypes.

evidence.snippet: novel therapeutic strategies have emerged, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), microRNA-based therapies, and interleukin-22 (IL-22)-mediated interventions, which show potential in targeting IR and metabolic dysfunction in PCOS.
evidence.explanation: Recent review establishes microRNA-based therapies as an emerging approach for PCOS with demonstrated potential in targeting insulin resistance and metabolic dysfunction. The cited sentence is the narrative review's own summary of an emerging therapeutic landscape rather than a result from a primary clinical study, so it is graded OTHER, consistent with this treatment's preclinical-stage notes.

treatments/11.description: MicroRNA-based therapies represent an emerging precision medicine approach targeting dysregulated miRNA expression in PCOS. MicroRNA modulation may address pathways affecting ovarian function, insulin signaling, and inflammation, offering a mechanistic intervention approach distinct from conventional hormone and metabolic therapies.

evidence.snippet: novel therapeutic strategies have emerged, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), microRNA-based therapies, and interleukin-22 (IL-22)-mediated interventions, which show potential in targeting IR and metabolic dysfunction in PCOS.
evidence.explanation: Recent review identifies IL-22-mediated interventions as an emerging therapeutic strategy with potential in PCOS pathophysiology. The cited sentence is the narrative review's own summary of an emerging therapeutic landscape rather than a result from a primary clinical study, so it is graded OTHER, consistent with this treatment's preclinical-stage notes.

treatments/12.description: IL-22-mediated interventions represent an emerging immunomodulatory approach to PCOS, targeting the IL-22 cytokine pathway to enhance metabolic and reproductive function. IL-22 signaling supports epithelial barrier integrity and metabolic homeostasis, with potential applications in addressing both metabolic dysfunction and chronic low-grade inflammation in PCOS.

evidence.snippet: modulation of gut microbiota through probiotics, prebiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) represents an emerging strategy for restoring metabolic homeostasis.
evidence.explanation: Recent review establishes microbiota modulation as an emerging therapeutic approach with potential for restoring metabolic homeostasis in PCOS. The quoted sentence is the review's forward-looking framing of a strategy that "represents an emerging" one, not a reported clinical result, so it is graded OTHER to match the three sibling emerging-therapy entries in this section and the entry's own notes.

treatments/13.description: Microbiota modulation through probiotics, prebiotics, and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) represents an emerging strategy for restoring metabolic homeostasis in PCOS. Dysbiosis-driven metabolic endotoxemia and altered short-chain fatty acid production contribute to PCOS pathophysiology, and microbiota restoration may improve insulin sensitivity, hormone metabolism, and reproductive function through multiple mechanisms.

evidence.snippet: Compelling evidence suggests that hyperandrogenism is not just a primary feature of PCOS. Instead, it may be a causative factor for this condition.
evidence.explanation: This review explicitly frames androgen excess as a possible causal driver, supporting the androgen-first hypothesis group.

evidence.snippet: However, the overexposure of androgen has direct and specific influence on the development of insulin resistance.
evidence.explanation: Supports the androgen-to-insulin-resistance arm of the proposed feedback model.

evidence.snippet: Global loss of the AR reveals that AR signaling is required for all DHT-induced features of PCOS.
evidence.explanation: Global androgen-receptor knockout in the DHT-induced mouse model shows the whole PCOS-like phenotype depends on androgen-receptor signalling, the strongest available causal test of the androgen arm of this hypothesis. Graded MODEL_ORGANISM: it is a mouse result and does not by itself establish androgen primacy in human PCOS.

evidence.snippet: Neuron-specific AR signaling was required for the development of dysfunctional ovulation, classic polycystic ovaries, reduced large antral follicle health, and several metabolic traits including obesity and dyslipidemia.
evidence.explanation: Locates the critical androgen-receptor target extraovarially, in neurons: the same cell-specific knockouts that prevent the reproductive phenotype also prevent obesity and dyslipidemia, which is why this entry routes the androgen arm through hypothalamic-pituitary dysregulation rather than asserting a direct ovarian-only mechanism.

evidence.snippet: We hypothesize that excess peripubertal androgens may reduce the sensitivity of the GnRH pulse generator to sex steroid inhibition in susceptible individuals, resulting in increased GnRH pulse frequency and subsequent abnormalities in gonadotropin secretion, ovarian androgen production, and ovulatory function.
evidence.explanation: States the androgen-first developmental sequence this hypothesis group encodes — peripubertal androgen excess desensitising the GnRH pulse generator. Cited as the review's own hypothesis, not as a demonstration: the authors frame it explicitly as a hypothesis, which is why this group remains ALTERNATIVE.

evidence.snippet: carriers of previously reported rare variants in DENND1A, a gene that regulates androgen biosynthesis, were significantly more likely to have the reproductive subtype of PCOS
evidence.explanation: Ties an intrinsic androgen-biosynthesis genotype to a reproductive (higher-LH, lower-BMI/insulin) phenotype cluster, the stratum in which the androgen-first ordering is most plausible.

evidence.snippet: Limitations of our study were that only PCOS cases of European ancestry diagnosed by National Institutes of Health (NIH) criteria were included, the sample sizes for the subtype GWAS were small, and the GWAS findings were not replicated.
evidence.explanation: The authors' own limitations statement, curated so the subtype restriction above is not read as a settled population prevalence or a validated androgen-first subtype.

hypotheses/0.description: Intrinsic ovarian/adrenal androgen excess, potentially reinforced by heightened LH action and theca-cell steroidogenic machinery, is the initiating lesion. Androgen excess then promotes insulin resistance and hyperinsulinemia, disrupts hypothalamic steroid feedback, and contributes to visceral adiposity, closing an androgen-insulin-adiposity feedback loop.

evidence.snippet: Hyperinsulinemia (i.e., elevated insulin without hypoglycemia) is a common metabolic feature of PCOS that worsens its reproductive symptoms by exacerbating pituitary hormone imbalances and increasing levels of bioactive androgens.
evidence.explanation: Supports hyperinsulinemia as an upstream amplifier of pituitary imbalance and bioactive androgen excess.

evidence.snippet: Insulin functions as a co-gonadotropin through its cognate receptor to modulate ovarian steroidogenesis.
evidence.explanation: Supports the ovarian steroidogenesis route by which hyperinsulinemia can increase androgen production.

evidence.snippet: In women with typical PCOS and normal insulin levels and metabolic insulin sensitivity, reducing insulin secretion significantly decreased androgen and increased SHBG levels.
evidence.explanation: Prospective insulin-lowering intervention: eight days of diazoxide lowered androgens and raised SHBG in lean PCOS women whose metabolic insulin sensitivity was normal, so an insulin contribution to hyperandrogenemia does not require measurable insulin resistance. Nine participants and no concurrent randomized control group, so this shows a contribution, not temporal primacy.

evidence.snippet: Insulin significantly increased AKR1C3 expression in differentiated subcutaneous adipocytes (p=0·04). Incubation with insulin significantly increased testosterone generation from androstenedione in cultured subcutaneous cell media compared with controls (p<0·001).
evidence.explanation: Identifies an extra-ovarian route from insulin to androgen: insulin induces AKR1C3 in subcutaneous adipocytes, which converts androstenedione to testosterone. Graded IN_VITRO because these two measurements are the cultured-adipocyte arm of the study.

evidence.snippet: Mendelian randomization analyses indicate causal roles in PCOS aetiology for higher BMI (P=2.5 × 10(-9)), higher insulin resistance (P=6 × 10(-4)) and lower serum sex hormone binding globulin concentrations (P=5 × 10(-4)).
evidence.explanation: Genetic instrumental-variable analysis in a European-ancestry GWAS infers a causal direction from insulin resistance (and BMI, and low SHBG) to PCOS, which is the strongest hypothesis-independent support for this group. The BMI effect is larger, so this supports insulin resistance as a causal contributor rather than as the sole initiating lesion.

hypotheses/1.description: Primary insulin resistance or primary hyperinsulinemia initiates the endocrine-metabolic loop. High insulin acts as a co-gonadotropin in the ovary and lowers hepatic SHBG, increasing bioactive androgen exposure; the resulting hyperandrogenism can then worsen insulin resistance and adiposity.

evidence.snippet: The majority of patients have elevated LH levels in plasma and a persistent rapid frequency of LH (GnRH) pulse secretion, the mechanisms of which are unclear.
evidence.explanation: Supports the upstream neuroendocrine abnormality represented by this hypothesis group.

evidence.snippet: These results suggest that although the elevated LH pulse frequency in PCOS may in part reflect impaired sensitivity to E2 and P, continuing actions of hyperandrogenemia are important for sustaining the abnormal hypothalamic sensitivity to feedback inhibition by ovarian steroids.
evidence.explanation: Supports the feedback component connecting androgen excess and persistent hypothalamic-pituitary dysregulation.

evidence.snippet: The NK3 receptor antagonist AZD4901 specifically reduced LH pulse frequency and subsequently serum LH and T concentrations, thus presenting NK3 receptor antagonism as a potential approach to treating the central neuroendocrine pathophysiology of PCOS.
evidence.explanation: Phase 2 placebo-controlled RCT pharmacologically validates the KNDy neuron -> GnRH/LH-pulse arm: blocking NK3 signaling lowers LH pulse frequency and downstream androgens in PCOS women.

evidence.snippet: Fezolinetant had a sustained effect to suppress hyperandrogenism and reduce the LH-to-FSH ratio in women with PCOS.
evidence.explanation: Independent phase 2a RCT of a second NK3-receptor antagonist replicates the neuroendocrine effect (reduced LH-to-FSH ratio and suppressed hyperandrogenism), reinforcing the KNDy/GnRH-pulse mechanism.

evidence.snippet: The same chr 11p14.1 SNP, rs11031006, in the region of the follicle-stimulating hormone B polypeptide (FSHB) gene strongly associates with PCOS diagnosis and luteinizing hormone levels. These findings implicate neuroendocrine changes in disease pathogenesis.
evidence.explanation: Unbiased European-ancestry GWAS links a gonadotropin-secretion (FSHB) locus to both PCOS diagnosis and LH levels, providing hypothesis-independent genetic support for a neuroendocrine contribution.

evidence.snippet: These data show that reduced PR signalling in the ARC of adult female mice is sufficient to drive hyperactivity within the HPG axis and mimic some but not all reproductive features of PCOS.
evidence.explanation: Targeted arcuate progesterone-receptor knockdown demonstrates that loss of progesterone negative feedback within arcuate GABAergic neurons is sufficient to raise LH pulse frequency, confirming a key node in the neuroendocrine causal chain.

evidence.snippet: There were no clinical or laboratory consequences of LH excess in this FSH-deficient woman. These findings support the hypothesis that excessive LH stimulation alone does not cause ovarian hyperandrogenism.
evidence.explanation: Qualifies the model: a woman with FSH-beta-deficiency-driven LH excess and PCOS-like LH pulse characteristics had normal androgens, showing that the neuroendocrine LH arm requires an intrinsic ovarian steroidogenic defect to produce hyperandrogenism.

evidence.snippet: LH pulse frequency and quantity of GnRH are increased in PCOS, but there is no influence of BMI on either marker of hypothalamic function. The pituitary response to a weight-based dose of GnRH is inversely related to BMI in PCOS.
evidence.explanation: Substantiates qualification (4) in this entry's notes, which was previously uncited: GnRH pulse frequency and drive are raised in PCOS irrespective of BMI, and it is the pituitary response that falls with rising BMI. So a normal serum LH in an obese patient does not exclude the hypothalamic abnormality this hypothesis group posits, and LH concentration is a poor proxy for it. Frequent-sampling and GnRH/antagonist testing in 24 women.

hypotheses/2.description: Impaired hypothalamic-pituitary sensitivity to ovarian steroid negative feedback maintains rapid LH/GnRH pulse secretion. Elevated LH signaling then drives theca-cell androgen biosynthesis, while androgen excess further impairs steroid feedback and can secondarily worsen insulin resistance.

evidence.snippet: our analyses reveal a predominant enrichment of metabolic dysregulation-associated pathways in East Asian PCOS, whereas European PCOS exhibits a stronger inflammatory and immune-related signature
evidence.explanation: Population-aware gene prioritization framework combining regulatory genomics, QTLs, and protein networks reveals distinct pathway enrichment patterns: East Asian PCOS driven by metabolic dysfunction, European PCOS by inflammation/immunity, with implications for subtype-specific therapeutics.

evidence.snippet: These population-specific molecular phenotypes were further supported by transcriptomic data from PCOS patient samples
evidence.explanation: Patient transcriptome data validate population-stratified pathway enrichment, confirming mechanistic divergence between East Asian and European PCOS cohorts rather than technical artifacts.

hypotheses/3.description: PCOS pathophysiology exhibits significant population-specific molecular phenotypes. East Asian populations show a predominant enrichment of metabolic dysregulation-associated pathways (insulin receptor signaling, GLUT4 translocation, metabolic syndrome), whereas European populations exhibit a stronger inflammatory and immune-related signature (NF-kB signaling, innate immunity, and interleukin/cytokine and inflammasome pathways). These population-specific mechanistic differences may drive differential therapeutic responsiveness and clinical phenotypes across ancestry groups.

evidence.snippet: Treatment remains ad hoc owing to limited understanding of underlying mechanisms, highlighting the need for research delineating the aetiology and pathophysiology of the syndrome.
evidence.explanation: The Disease Primer frames unresolved PCOS mechanisms as a research need, supporting the explicit knowledge-gap discussion.

evidence.snippet: Considering the heterogeneous nature of PCOS, it is improbable that its metabolic characteristics always follow the same progression.
evidence.explanation: Supports subtype-specific causal hierarchy rather than a single universal insulin-resistance sequence.

evidence.snippet: Cluster C (43.3%) showed lower BP, BMI, HOMA-IR, triglycerides, testosterone, and FAI and higher LH: FSH, DHEAS, androstenedione, 17-hydroxyprogesterone, SHBG, and HDL.
evidence.explanation: The largest cluster in a 975-patient NIH-defined cohort combines low insulin resistance with a high LH:FSH ratio, so no single insulin-first or adiposity-first ordering can hold across the syndrome. The measurements are contemporaneous and cross-sectional, so this establishes stratum heterogeneity, not which mechanism initiates in that stratum — which is exactly the gap stated here.

evidence.snippet: Hormonal regulation in the etiology of this condition, through metabolic and reproductive features, was emphasized. The proteomic analysis highlighted metabolic biology known to be related to PCOS.
evidence.explanation: The largest PCOS genetic study to date (n = 544,513, 29 loci) implicates reproductive/hormonal and metabolic biology together rather than resolving to one, which is hypothesis-independent evidence that the causal-hierarchy question posed here is not settled by genetics.

open_questions/0.rationale: Current evidence supports bidirectional reinforcement among androgen excess, hyperinsulinemia/insulin resistance, and adiposity, but it does not establish a single causal sequence that applies across lean and obese PCOS. The entry therefore models three competing or superimposed hypothesis groups and annotates causal edges by subgroup.

evidence.snippet: The mechanism underlying granulosa cell apoptosis in polycystic ovary syndrome remains unclear.
evidence.explanation: Directly states the unresolved mechanism that this knowledge-gap discussion captures.

evidence.snippet: Results demonstrated that elevated PCSK9 levels induce lipid metabolism abnormalities in PCOS mice, subsequently activating AMP-activated protein kinase and glycogen synthase kinase 3β within follicles.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the proposed PCSK9 -> lipid abnormality -> AMPK/GSK-3beta cascade in PCOS model mice that the gap and proposed experiments interrogate for human translatability.

open_questions/1.rationale: Granulosa cell death is recognized as one of the primary factors impairing follicular growth, development, and oocyte maturation in PCOS, yet its upstream pathological triggers have been poorly defined. Teng et al. (2026) propose a specific cascade in which elevated proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type-9 (PCSK9) drives lipid metabolism abnormalities that activate AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and glycogen synthase kinase 3beta (GSK-3beta) within follicles, triggering granulosa cell apoptosis and impairing ovarian function. Several questions remain unresolved. First, the cascade was established in PCOS model mice and primary follicles, so whether elevated PCSK9 is a primary driver in human PCOS rather than a species- or model-specific finding is unknown. Second, the proximal mechanism by which PCSK9-driven lipid abnormalities impair granulosa cell survival (intracellular lipid-droplet accumulation versus altered membrane lipid composition versus lipotoxic oxidative stress) is undefined. Third, it is unclear whether AMPK/GSK-3beta is the dominant death pathway or whether it operates in parallel with the previously modeled ferroptosis-autophagy crosstalk and ER/oxidative-stress programs that also drive granulosa cell loss. Resolving the relative contribution and translatability of these death pathways would clarify whether PCSK9 inhibition is a viable PCOS-directed therapeutic target.

evidence.snippet: integration of genetic evidence with a network-based approach enabled the identification of druggable targets lacking direct genetic cues
evidence.explanation: Network-based gene prioritization strategy identifies population-specific druggable targets and therapeutic candidates that would not emerge from genetic associations alone, laying a foundation for ancestry-informed precision therapeutics.

open_questions/2.rationale: Population-stratified mechanistic analyses reveal that East Asian PCOS is enriched for metabolic dysregulation pathways while European PCOS exhibits stronger inflammatory and immune signatures. The heterogeneous molecular architecture suggests that therapeutic responses may vary by ancestry, yet current PCOS treatment guidelines do not account for mechanistic diversity. Whether therapies targeting the predominant mechanism in each population (e.g., metabolic pathway inhibitors for East Asian PCOS, anti-inflammatory agents for European PCOS) would improve clinical outcomes relative to universal treatment remains untested.
